increments.title: Add the FIT Tests job to check-pull-request.yml
increments.detail: check-pull-request.yml has no FIT job: animals runs a separate playwright job (npm run playwright:install, npm run test:fit:ci, uploads playwright-report/ and test-results/ for 14 days) so the frontend-owned Playwright projects run on every PR without a stack; plants has the test:fit:ci script but nothing calls it. The job's steps are, in order: `actions/checkout@v7`; `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc` and `cache: npm`; `npm install --global "$(node scripts/npm-version.js)"` named "Align npm with the version pinned in package.json"; `npm ci`; `npm run playwright:install`; `npm run test:fit:ci` (animals check-pull-request.yml:97-118). scripts/npm-version.js and .nvmrc both already exist in the plants repo, so the npm-alignment step is copied verbatim, not adapted

The final step uploads the report with `if: always()`, `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `name: frontend-playwright-report`, `path:` the two lines `playwright-report/` and `test-results/`, and `retention-days: 14` (animals check-pull-request.yml:120-128; backlog-extras.json ci-fit-job "uploads playwright-report/ and test-results/ for 14 days")

The job calls the plants repo's own `test:fit:ci` script unchanged — package.json already defines `test:fit:ci` as `PORT=3053 npm run test:fit -- --retries=2 --forbid-only --global-timeout=900000 --reporter=list,html,github` and `playwright:install` as `playwright install --with-deps chromium`. Neither script, nor playwright.config.js, is edited: the extra's complaint is that "plants has the test:fit:ci script but nothing calls it" (backlog-extras.json ci-fit-job)

A comment above the job records why it is a separate job from pr-validator — the frontend owns the `features` and `journeys` Playwright projects, which boot the app themselves and need no workspace stack, and a browser run is kept out of the way of the PR checks (animals check-pull-request.yml:87-92; both projects use devices['Desktop Chrome'] per plants playwright.config.js:30,51, which is why only chromium is installed)

Nothing else in the file changes: the `security-audit` step stays inside pr-validator (inc-003 ci-security-audit-non-gating owns splitting it out), no `schedule:`/cron trigger is added (inc-004 ci-weekly-schedule owns it), and the commented-out SonarCloud block stays commented (inc-005 ci-sonarcloud owns it). The workflow file still parses as valid YAML and the two jobs remain independent (no `needs:` between `pr-validator` and `playwright`)
openQuestions: The target profile's commitPaths for high-risk-plants-frontend are only `src/server/app` and `package.json`, and commit-increment.sh runs `git add` against exactly those paths (tools/journey-builder/commit-increment.sh:33) while rollback-increment.sh checks out and cleans only those (rollback-increment.sh:32-33). A `.github/workflows/` edit therefore will not be staged, committed or rolled back. This affects inc-002 through inc-011 (every ci-* extra) and inc-001 (scripts/lighthouse/). Either commitPaths gains `.github` and `scripts`, or the loop needs an explicit extra-paths escape for repo-hygiene increments. The implementor cannot resolve this from inside the repo.

increments.title: Split security-audit out of pr-validator as a non-gating job
increments.detail: security-audit is a step INSIDE pr-validator, so any new advisory blocks the merge check; animals keeps Security audit as a separate non-gating job for exactly that reason. Move it to its own job mirroring animals check-pull-request.yml. Evidence: skeleton ci-fit-and-audit-jobs (2).

filesToTouch.what: delete the 'Security audit' step from pr-validator and add a top-level `security-audit` job that mirrors animals'

acceptanceCriteria: The `pr-validator` job no longer contains the two-line `- name: Security audit` / `run: npm run security-audit` step it holds today (plants .github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml:40-41); its remaining steps are unchanged in order and content — Checkout code, the setup-node step, 'Align npm with the version pinned in package.json', 'Install dependencies', the build/format:check/lint/test run block, 'Test Docker Image Build' with tag trade-imports-plants-frontend, and the commented-out SonarCloud block

A new top-level job `security-audit` exists with `name: Security audit` and `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, whose steps mirror animals check-pull-request.yml:67-87 exactly: 'Checkout code' (actions/checkout@v7); 'Set up Node' (actions/setup-node@v7, `node-version-file: .nvmrc`, `cache: npm`); 'Align npm with the version pinned in package.json' (`run: npm install --global "$(node scripts/npm-version.js)"`); 'Install dependencies' (`run: npm ci`); 'Security audit' (`run: npm run security-audit`)

The `security-audit` job declares no `needs:` and no other job declares `needs: security-audit`, so the audit runs in parallel and a new advisory cannot turn the merge check red — the whole point of the split (backlog-extras.json ci-security-audit-non-gating; skeleton ci-fit-and-audit-jobs (2): 'animals keeps Security audit as a separate non-gating job for exactly that reason')

A comment above the job records why it is a separate job — that `npm audit` scans the installed tree against a live advisory feed, so a newly published advisory would otherwise turn every open PR red regardless of what the PR changed, and block the very PR carrying the fix (mirrors animals check-pull-request.yml:60-66). This is a CI-policy rationale a future reader would otherwise undo, not an explanatory code comment

`security-audit` is placed between `pr-validator` and the `playwright` / 'FIT Tests' job that inc-002 added, matching animals' file order (animals: pr-validator :16, security-audit :67, playwright :93)

package.json is not touched: `security-audit` stays `npm audit --audit-level=high` (plants package.json scripts.security-audit) and the job invokes it through `npm run security-audit`, never a raw `npm audit`
The file parses as valid YAML with exactly three top-level jobs — `pr-validator`, `security-audit`, `playwright` — and the `on:` block is untouched (inc-004 owns adding the schedule cron)

The split only makes the audit non-gating if it is NOT required; that setting lives in GitHub, not in the repo, and neither the spec nor the skeleton records it. If it is required, the fix is cosmetic until someone unticks it.

increments.title: Fix the literal concurrency group in publish.yml and publish-hotfix.yml
increments.detail: Both publish workflows carry a concurrency block whose group is the literal string '21660{{ github.workflow }}' (double dollar — the expression is never evaluated) with queue: max; animals has no such block. Either evaluate the expression properly or drop the block. Evidence: skeleton ci-publish-arm64-missing (publish.yml:8-11; publish-hotfix.yml:6-9).

filesToTouch.what: in the concurrency block (lines 8-11): drop the escaping `$` from the group expression and delete the inert `queue: max` line
in the concurrency block (lines 6-9): drop the escaping `$` from the group expression and delete the inert `queue: max` line

acceptanceCriteria: publish.yml's concurrency block reads exactly `concurrency:` / `  group: ${{ github.workflow }}` / `  cancel-in-progress: false` — one `$`, not two. Today it reads `group: $${{ github.workflow }}` (plants .github/workflows/publish.yml:9); `$${{ ... }}` is GitHub's documented escape for a literal `${{ ... }}`, so the group is the eleven-character-plus literal string rather than an evaluated expression (backlog-extras.json ci-publish-concurrency-group)

publish-hotfix.yml's concurrency block reads exactly `concurrency:` / `  group: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}` / `  cancel-in-progress: false`. Today it reads `group: $${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}` (plants .github/workflows/publish-hotfix.yml:7). This is the file where the defect bites: with the literal, every hotfix branch shares one concurrency group and queues behind every other; evaluated, each branch gets its own group, which is what the expression was written to do

The `queue: max` line is deleted from both blocks (publish.yml:11, publish-hotfix.yml:9). GitHub Actions' `concurrency` schema defines only `group` and `cancel-in-progress`; `queue` is neither, and it is provably inert rather than fatal — the plants Publish run for PR #4 on 2026-09-06 concluded `success` with the key present, so GitHub accepts and ignores it. Deleting it changes no behaviour and removes dead config from the two files this increment already opens

`cancel-in-progress: false` is kept in both files. It is the GitHub default, but the explicit line is the record that a publish must never be cancelled mid-flight — cdp-build-action bumps the version and pushes a tag, so a cancelled run can leave the tag ahead of the image

The concurrency block is kept in both files rather than deleted. The extra offers both options ('Either evaluate the expression properly or drop the block') and no decision in decisions.json rules between them; the ruling recorded in `notes` is to fix, not drop, so serialisation of publishes to main survives

No other line in either file changes. In particular inc-005's uncommented SonarCloud step and inc-006's `publish-arm64` job (needs: build, uses DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace/.github/workflows/publish-multiarch.yml@main) are already in publish.yml when this increment starts and must come through untouched, as must both files' `on:`, `permissions:` and `env:` blocks and the `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: '094954420758'` quoting
`.github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml` is not touched — it carries no concurrency block (verified by grep), so it has nothing for this increment to fix

No explanatory comment is added above either block. The corrected expression states its own intent; the reason for keeping the block rather than dropping it belongs in the commit message, not the workflow file (workspace rule: remove explanatory comments aggressively)
After the edit, `grep -rn 'queue:' .github/workflows/` in the plants frontend returns nothing, and `grep -rn '[$][$][{][{]' .github/workflows/` returns nothing
Both files still parse as valid YAML with two-space indentation matching their surroundings, and each concurrency block is three lines where it was four
openQuestions: Whether `queue: max` is a CDP platform extension rather than scaffold noise. It is not in GitHub's concurrency schema and the 2026-09-06 Publish run succeeded with it present, so it is inert on GitHub's side — but it appears identically in five sibling DEFRA repos (trade-imports-address-book publish.yml:11 and publish-hotfix.yml:9, trade-imports-plants-backend publish.yml:11 and publish-hotfix.yml:9, trade-imports-ins-frontend publish.yml:11, trade-imports-ins-backend publish.yml:11 and publish-hotfix.yml:9), which reads like a CDP template rather than a local typo. Nothing in the spec, the repos or CDP's documentation in this workspace records a contract that reads the key. If CDP's own tooling does read it, dropping it changes CDP-side queuing.

Whether the same fix should sweep the five sibling repos that carry the identical `$${{` escape and `queue: max`. Out of scope here: this increment's `repo` is `frontend` and CLAUDE.md rule 2 would put a cross-repo change on one shared branch name. Raise it separately if wanted.
increments.recipe: repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend/.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml:14-16 and repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend/.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml:14-16 (the in-workspace exemplar of a correctly written concurrency block — single `$`, no `queue` key)
increments.notes: RULED (planner, headless, EUDPA-409 inc-007): the extra offers 'evaluate the expression properly OR drop the block' and nothing in decisions.json rules between them, so this plan takes 'evaluate properly'. Dropping the block would match animals (whose publish.yml and publish-hotfix.yml carry no concurrency block — verified) but would remove a real property: with cdp-build-action bumping the version and pushing a tag on every push to main, two concurrent publishes can race the tag. Animals' absence of a block is the older CDP scaffold, not a ruling, and the standing consistency-with-animals rule in PROGRAMME-NOTES.md is about journey shape and copy, not CI config. Three discrepancies between the increment's own text and the files (the files win, and they were read at lines 8-11 and 6-9 as the evidence cites): (1) the detail quotes the group as the literal string '21660{{ github.workflow }}' — the file actually reads `$${{ github.workflow }}`, the '21660' being a corruption of `$$` in the skeleton extract; (2) the detail says BOTH workflows carry a group of `github.workflow`, but only publish.yml does — publish-hotfix.yml's expression is `github.head_ref || github.ref_name`, which is why the two files need different corrected values; (3) the detail treats both as equally broken, but publish.yml's defect is cosmetic — `github.workflow` evaluates to the constant 'Publish', so literal and evaluated both yield one constant group — while publish-hotfix.yml's is functional, collapsing every hotfix branch into one queue. Say so in the PR body; do not let a reviewer read the publish.yml half as a behaviour change. Sequencing: inc-005 (SonarCloud uncomment) and inc-006 (publish-arm64 job) both land in publish.yml before this increment, but both touch the bottom of the file while this touches lines 8-11, so no conflict is expected; inc-008 (publish-branch.yml) creates a new file after this and should copy the corrected three-line block, not the four-line one. Ladder: the fit rung is deliberately off it — for a CI-workflow-only change the rungs are unit, format and lint locally, with the PR's own checks (which the loop watches) as the real proof; the Publish workflow itself only runs on merge to main, so the first live proof is the post-merge run. format:check does not cover .yml (its globs are js/cjs/md/json/config.js/test.js), so match the surrounding two-space indentation by hand.

increments.title: Add lighthouse.yml (Lighthouse CI on workflow_run of Publish Branch Image)
increments.detail: No .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml. Animals' runs on workflow_run of 'Publish Branch Image' or dispatch, reports a pending status, checks out the workspace, starts the stack for the branch, runs npm run lighthouse, tears the stack down, uploads the report for 14 days, publishes to GitHub Pages and passes result/report URL/flagged findings to the workspace status action. Depends on lighthouse-scripts and ci-publish-branch-workflow. Evidence: skeleton ci-lighthouse-workflow-missing (animals lighthouse.yml:1-40; docs/lighthouse.md CI ownership).

filesToTouch.what: the Lighthouse CI workflow: workflow_run of "Publish Branch Image" plus dispatch, pending-status job, lighthouse-test job (workspace checkout, branch tag, stack up, frontend install, npm run lighthouse, report index, flagged findings, artifact, teardown), lighthouse-publish job to GitHub Pages and report-status job
rewrite the 'CI ownership' section: the workflow now exists in this repository; say what it does and what remains true (nothing to audit until the first journey page lands)

acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml is created with `name: Lighthouse CI` and triggers `workflow_run` (`workflows: ["Publish Branch Image"]`, `types: [completed]`) and `workflow_dispatch` carrying one optional string input `branch` described 'Branch name to probe for service images (defaults to current branch)' (animals lighthouse.yml:1-12; backlog-extras.json ci-lighthouse-workflow "runs on workflow_run of 'Publish Branch Image' or dispatch")

It declares `concurrency: { group: lighthouse-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || github.ref_name }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` and top-level `permissions: contents: write, checks: write, pull-requests: write` — the check run, the PR comment and the gh-pages push all need them (animals lighthouse.yml:14-21)

Job `pending-status`, gated `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`, runs on ubuntu-latest and has one step using `DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace/.github/actions/report-lighthouse-status@main` with `lighthouse-result: pending` (animals lighthouse.yml:24-33; action.yml:4-7; extra detail "reports a pending status")

Job `lighthouse-test`, gated `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request')`, runs on ubuntu-latest with `timeout-minutes: 30` and exposes `outputs.tag` from the branch-tag step (animals lighthouse.yml:35-43)

Its steps are the animals steps in the animals order: checkout the workspace (`actions/checkout@v7`, `repository: DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace`, `ref: main`); the `branch-tag` id step whose sanitiser is copied character for character (slashes to hyphens, non-[a-zA-Z0-9_.-] stripped, lowercased, leading . or - trimmed, truncated to 128, written to $GITHUB_OUTPUT); `./scripts/stack/run-stack.sh --branch "${{ inputs.branch || github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || github.ref_name }}"` (animals lighthouse.yml:45-63; extra detail "checks out the workspace, starts the stack for the branch")

Then: checkout `DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend` at the same branch expression into `path: frontend`; `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc`, `cache: npm`, `cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json`; `npm install --global "$(node scripts/npm-version.js)"` and `npm ci`, both `working-directory: frontend` — plants pins `packageManager: npm@11.6.2` and carries scripts/npm-version.js, and check-pull-request.yml:34-38 uses the same two steps for the same reason (animals lighthouse.yml:65-88)

Then `npm run lighthouse` with `id: lhci` and `working-directory: frontend` (animals lighthouse.yml:90-93; extra detail "runs npm run lighthouse"). No `LIGHTHOUSE_BASE_URL` is set: the stack serves plants-frontend on port 3003 (docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:139,163) and lighthouserc.cjs already defaults there, so an override would only introduce drift

Then, `if: always() && steps.lhci.outcome != 'skipped'`, the report-index step (the inline `node -e` that reads `./frontend/lighthouse-report/manifest.json`, keeps `isRepresentativeRun` entries and writes `./frontend/lighthouse-report/index.html` with the performance / accessibility / best-practices columns — three categories, no SEO column) and `node scripts/lighthouse/flag-simple-findings.cjs` with `working-directory: frontend` (animals lighthouse.yml:95-120; the script exists in plants at scripts/lighthouse/flag-simple-findings.cjs and writes lighthouse-report/flagged-audits.json, docs/lighthouse.md:95-103)

Then, `if: always()`, `actions/upload-artifact@v7` with `name: lighthouse-report`, `path: frontend/lighthouse-report/`, `retention-days: 14`, and last `docker compose -p trade-imports down` — the workspace stack's compose project is literally `trade-imports` (docker/stack/compose.yml:1), so the teardown line is copied unchanged (animals lighthouse.yml:122-132; extra detail "tears the stack down, uploads the report for 14 days")

Job `lighthouse-publish` with `needs: lighthouse-test`, `if: always() && needs.lighthouse-test.result != 'skipped' && needs.lighthouse-test.result != 'cancelled'`, `permissions: contents: write`, `concurrency: { group: pages-${{ github.repository }}, cancel-in-progress: false }`: it downloads the artifact (`actions/download-artifact@v8`), deploys with `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4` to `destination_dir: lighthouse/${{ needs.lighthouse-test.outputs.tag }}` with `keep_files: false`, and outputs `report-url` built from the lowercased owner as `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/lighthouse/<tag>/` (animals lighthouse.yml:134-174; extra detail "publishes to GitHub Pages"). The owner/repo are taken from `github.repository` at run time, so no plants literal is hard-coded

Job `report-status` with `needs: [lighthouse-test, lighthouse-publish]`, gated `if: always() && github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`: it downloads the artifact with `continue-on-error: true` when lighthouse-test succeeded or failed, then calls `report-lighthouse-status@main` with `lighthouse-result: ${{ needs.lighthouse-test.result }}`, `report-url: ${{ needs.lighthouse-publish.outputs.report-url }}` and `flagged-audits-path: lighthouse-report/flagged-audits.json` — exactly three of the action's four inputs, `max-flagged-per-category` left at its default of 5 (animals lighthouse.yml:176-197; action.yml:4-19; extra detail "passes result/report URL/flagged findings to the workspace status action")

The only plants adaptation anywhere in the file is `repository: DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend` in the Checkout frontend step. Every other line is the animals file as it stands: paths, script names, the compose project and the report layout are all already correct for plants

The `workflows: ["Publish Branch Image"]` trigger name matches, character for character, the `name:` of the publish-branch.yml inc-008 added (animals publish-branch.yml:1). If what actually landed on the branch differs, this file matches what is there — a mismatch silently means the workflow never fires

It records that the workflow now exists and what it does (workflow_run after a successful branch image publish or manual dispatch; workspace checkout, stack for the branch, install, `npm run lighthouse`, always tear down, 14-day artifact, GitHub Pages, result / report URL / flagged findings to the workspace status action), keeps the closing guidance to reproduce a CI failure against the same route and stack before changing code or limits, and drops the 'Plants needs the same workflow' paragraph. It states what stays true: there is nothing to audit until the first journey page lands (docs/lighthouse.md:105-119; inc-001 plan criterion 'CI ownership stays open until inc-011 adds lighthouse.yml')

No other file changes: package.json, lighthouserc.cjs, scripts/lighthouse/, src/ and the existing workflows (check-pull-request.yml, publish.yml, publish-hotfix.yml, publish-branch.yml, e2e-tests.yml, cleanup-e2e-reports.yml) are untouched. The floors stay where inc-001 left them — no assertion is added, changed or relaxed here, and no SEO assertion is introduced
The file parses as valid YAML and keeps the four-job dependency shape: `pending-status` and `lighthouse-test` independent, `lighthouse-publish` needs `lighthouse-test`, `report-status` needs both
openQuestions: GitHub Pages on DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend. lighthouse-publish pushes to the gh-pages branch with peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4 and emits https://defra.github.io/trade-imports-plants-frontend/lighthouse/<branch-tag>/ as the report URL the PR check links to. The action creates the branch, but unless Pages is enabled for the repo that URL 404s. A repository setting, not a change the implementor can make in the diff. Whether a red Lighthouse check should block plants PRs before the first journey page exists. The set registers no routes yet (features/index.js exports allRoutes = []), so lighthouse:targets writes no URLs and lighthouserc.cjs:22-24 throws 'lists no URLs' — the check will conclude failure on every plants PR until the first page increment lands in M1. increments.title: Enable Dependabot in the plants frontend
increments.detail: .github/ holds only example.dependabot.yml (the CDP template). Add .github/dependabot.yml copied from animals: daily 10:30 Europe/London, one rolling patch-and-minor group over '*' excluding govuk-frontend (its own CHANGELOG-driven upgrade), majors raised individually, eslint ignored, direct deps only, plus the same policy for github-actions. Evidence: skeleton dependabot-absent (animals .github/dependabot.yml:1-69).

filesToTouch.what: the live Dependabot config: npm and github-actions ecosystems, one rolling patch-and-minor group each, daily 10:30 Europe/London
the superseded CDP template — animals removed it in the same commit that added dependabot.yml (827ab96b, recorded by git as a rename R091)

acceptanceCriteria: `.github/dependabot.yml` is created and does not exist before this increment (`ls .github/` today: example.dependabot.yml, workflows/). The file opens `version: 2` and carries exactly two `updates:` entries, `package-ecosystem: npm` then `package-ecosystem: github-actions`, both `directory: /` (animals .github/dependabot.yml:1-6, :49-50)

npm entry: `open-pull-requests-limit: 10` (animals :7); a single group `patch-and-minor` with `applies-to: version-updates`, `update-types: ['patch', 'minor']`, `patterns: ['*']` and `exclude-patterns: ['govuk-frontend']` (animals :21-30). The exclusion is the increment's stated requirement — govuk-frontend has its own CHANGELOG-driven upgrade (the `govuk-upgrade` skill) — and it bites here because govuk-frontend is a direct runtime dependency of the plants frontend (package.json dependencies, `^6.3.0`)

npm entry keeps `ignore:` for `'eslint-*'` and `'eslint'` (animals :32-34; identical in the plants template it replaces, example.dependabot.yml:52-54), `versioning-strategy: increase` (animals :42) and `allow: - dependency-type: direct` (animals :44-46). The detail's 'majors raised individually' is achieved by the group matching only patch and minor — no major group is added and the PR limit is not changed to force it

Both entries schedule `interval: daily`, `time: '10:30'`, `timezone: 'Europe/London'` (animals :36-40, :65-69). This is the one behavioural change from the plants template, which is `interval: weekly` on both (example.dependabot.yml:56-60, :72-76)

github-actions entry carries the same `patch-and-minor` group — `applies-to: version-updates`, `update-types: ['patch', 'minor']`, `patterns: ['*']`, no `exclude-patterns` and no `open-pull-requests-limit` (animals :56-63). The plants template has no groups on this ecosystem at all; adding it is 'plus the same policy for github-actions' from the detail

The five pattern groups in the plants template — `build`, `lint`, `logging`, `tools`, `types` (example.dependabot.yml:10-50) — are gone, replaced by the single update-type group. Do not carry any of them over and do not merge them into the new group: animals' comment (:9-20) records why grouping by update type beats a pattern list ('@vitest/coverage-v8' escaped the old 'vitest-*' pattern), and the plants template carries that same 'vitest-*' pattern (example.dependabot.yml:39) with the same escape

The two explanatory comment blocks are copied with the file (animals :9-20 above the npm group, :52-55 above the github-actions group) — they are the rationale for the update-type grouping and the govuk-frontend exclusion, and this repo has nowhere else that records it

`.github/example.dependabot.yml` is deleted. Animals did exactly this: commit 827ab96b ('Added the Dependabot configuration to enable dependabot on a daily basis') is recorded by git as `R091 .github/example.dependabot.yml -> .github/dependabot.yml`, and animals' `.github/` today holds only `dependabot.yml` and `workflows/`. Across the workspace no repo holds both files — the six repos with a live config have no template, the five without have only the template. Leaving the template beside the live file would leave a stale config contradicting it

No README change. Animals' same commit also edited its README `### Dependabot` section, but the plants README has no Dependabot section and no mention of dependabot anywhere: the only `dependabot` strings in the whole plants frontend are `.github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml` and four files under the set's `spec/`. Do not add a section — documentation gaps in this repo belong to inc-017 (docs-drift-sweep)

No other file changes. The one other `dependabot` reference in the repo is the commented-out `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'` guard on the SonarCloud step (check-pull-request.yml:56) — that line belongs to inc-005 (ci-sonarcloud) and is not touched here

Nothing under `src/` is touched: the unit and lint rungs are unaffected, and `format:check`'s globs (`src/**/*.js` and `**/*.{js,cjs,md,json,config.js,test.js}` — plants package.json) do not cover `.yml`, so the new file is never prettier-formatted; match the two-space indentation and single-quoted scalars of the animals original by hand
openQuestions: A `dependabot.yml` only takes effect if the dependency graph and Dependabot version updates are enabled on DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend at repo or org level. The checkout cannot see that setting, and a config GitHub is not reading produces no PRs and no error. Like the other M0 platform questions, this resolves on the platform after merge — check the repo's Insights, Dependency graph, Dependabot tab for the parsed config and the first daily run; if it is off, that is a repo-settings question for Sam, not a change to this file.

Its sibling inc-013 does the same job in the plants backend from a different animals source; no shared file, no ordering between them. The detail's phrase 'majors raised individually' describes an effect, not a second group: majors match no group and Dependabot raises them one per PR — do not add a majors group to make the words literal. Second of the two Dependabot increments and the FIRST increment of this backlog in the plants BACKEND — the twelve before it are all in the plants frontend. dependsOn inc-012, which does the same job in the plants frontend: a different repo, so the dependency is ordering and reviewer consistency, not a file conflict, and nothing inc-012 creates is edited here.

Discrepancy between the increment's own text and the evidence, and the resolution. (1) The detail says "mirroring the animals backend policy (maven + github-actions)", but the animals backend's live dependabot.yml:4 declares `nuget`, not `maven`, and that repo has no .csproj or .sln anywhere — its only manifest is pom.xml. Commit 5ba526a renamed the CDP template into place with zero content change, so the ecosystem was never corrected and has never updated a Java dependency there. Do NOT copy `nuget`: the detail's parenthetical is the requirement, the ecosystem is `maven`, and dynamics-gateway is the workspace's proof of the corrected shape. The animals-backend `nuget` entry is a real defect but it is out of scope here and is NOT a reason to touch the animals repo in this increment. (2) The detail says only "Add .github/dependabot.yml" and is silent on the template it supersedes and on the README; the evidence settles both — 5ba526a is a git rename and it edited README.md in the same commit, and no repo in this workspace holds both files. Unlike its sibling inc-012 (whose plan rules 'No README change' because the plants FRONTEND README has no Dependabot section at all), the plants backend README does carry the CDP section and would be left stating a falsehood, so the README edit is in scope here. inc-017 (docs-drift-sweep) cannot pick it up: that extra's repo is `frontend`.

inc-014 (backend-ci-parity) follows immediately and adds e2e-tests.yml, publish-branch.yml, cleanup-e2e-reports.yml and a publish-arm64 job to this repo's .github/workflows/, and restores the sonarcloud calls. The `github-actions` entry landing here needs no revision when they arrive — it globs `/`. Landing this first is deliberate: the action pins are already inconsistent (actions/checkout@v5 in check-pull-request.yml:20, publish.yml:29 and publish-hotfix.yml:26 but @v4 in sonarcloud.yml:16), so Dependabot has real work from day one. `DEFRA/cdp-build-action/build@main` (publish.yml:42) and `build-hotfix@main` are branch refs Dependabot will not bump; that is expected and matches animals.

Once this merges, every weekly bot PR runs check-pull-request.yml, whose `Run tests with Testcontainers` step is `mvn clean verify` followed by a full `docker build --no-cache`. Animals accepts the same cost; no guard is added here.

The local rung needs Docker running: the integration tests are Testcontainers-backed (pom.xml, src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/plants/integration/IntegrationBase.java, MongoConfigIT.java) and `mvn test` alone would skip Failsafe, so the ladder is `mvn ... clean verify` and nothing lighter. There is no maven wrapper at the repo root, so `mvn` comes from PATH. No frontend rung applies — this increment touches no JavaScript, so `test:high-risk-plants`, `format:check` and `lint` have nothing to say about it — and the fit rung is off the ladder for the same reason it is off inc-002 to inc-011: a config file changes no runtime behaviour a browser run could observe. The PR's own checks, which the loop watches, are the real proof.

M0 hygiene: no journey code, no obligation, no copy, no Welsh, and no interaction with the copy-convention or copy-parity tripwires, which live in the frontend and are not armed until the first feature increment. The spec ties in only through behaviour `nfr-sustainable` / d-081, which parks Annex 6's unqualified 'Sustainable' and records that if policy ever means maintainability then this extra already serves it — a fact kept in the ledger, not a requirement, and no increment follows from it. commitPaths already covers `.github`, `docs` and `README.md` for this target and is not the orchestrator's concern (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md).

increments.title: Bring the plants backend CI to parity with the animals backend

(animals publish.yml:39-45). publish.yml's commented-out block at :45-53 — the four `##` prose lines and the five `#` job lines keyed `sonarcloud-scan` — is deleted outright and replaced by the animals shape: a live job keyed `sonarcloud` with `name: SonarCloud Scan`, `needs: build`, `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`, `uses: ./.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml`, `secrets: inherit` (animals publish.yml:47-52). The job key and name are animals' (`sonarcloud` / "SonarCloud Scan"), not the commented block's (`sonarcloud-scan` / "CDP SonarCloud Scan") — parity is with the live animals file, not with the dead CDP template text. No commented-out remnant is left behind

check-pull-request.yml's commented-out inline step at :37-42 (`#      - name: SonarCloud Scan` through `#          SONAR_TOKEN: ...`, using SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@v5) is deleted outright, not uncommented. Animals does not run the scanner action inline; it calls the reusable workflow as a job, and the plants repo already has that workflow (sonarcloud.yml) with the Maven scanner and the coverage exclusions the inline action would not apply

check-pull-request.yml gains a top-level `sonarcloud` job as a sibling of `pr-validator`, exactly `name: SonarCloud Scan`, `needs: pr-validator`, `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`, `uses: ./.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml`, `secrets: inherit` (animals check-pull-request.yml:38-43). `needs: pr-validator` matters: the scan is a second full `mvn clean verify`, and gating it on the cheap check keeps a broken PR from paying for both

The `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'` guard is present on both new sonarcloud jobs. It is the extra's own wording ("skipped for dependabot") and it is load-bearing from the moment inc-013's `.github/dependabot.yml` starts raising weekly PRs: `secrets: inherit` does not reach a Dependabot-actor run, so an unguarded job fails on an empty SONAR_TOKEN every Monday

sonarcloud.yml's Set up Java step reads `java-version-file: .java-version` in place of `java-version: 25` (plants sonarcloud.yml:24), matching animals sonarcloud.yml:20-25. Unquoted, like the `distribution: corretto` and `cache: maven` around it in that file — not `'.java-version'`, which is the quoting the other two plants workflows use. `.java-version` today contains `25`, so this changes no behaviour now; it stops the scan silently building on a different JDK from the build the next time that file moves

sonarcloud.yml is otherwise unchanged: `on: workflow_call:` only, the `fetch-depth: 0` checkout, the Sonar cache steps, and the analyze step's `-Dsonar.projectKey=DEFRA_trade-imports-plants-backend` with its exclusions (:44) all stay. In particular `actions/checkout@v4` at :16 is left as it is — animals pins @v4 in the same file, and action-version pins are Dependabot's job now that inc-013 has landed the `github-actions` ecosystem entry

publish.yml's concurrency block reads exactly `concurrency:` / `  group: ${{ github.workflow }}` / `  cancel-in-progress: false` — one `$`, not two, and no `queue:` line. Today it is `group: $${{ github.workflow }}` with `queue: max` (plants publish.yml:8-11); `$${{ ... }}` is GitHub's documented escape for a literal `${{ ... }}`, so the group is a literal string rather than an evaluated expression, and `queue` is not a key in the Actions `concurrency` schema

publish-hotfix.yml's concurrency block reads exactly `concurrency:` / `  group: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}` / `  cancel-in-progress: false` (today :6-9). This is where the literal bites: unevaluated, every hotfix branch shares one group and queues behind every other; evaluated, each branch gets its own, which is what the expression was written to do

The concurrency blocks are kept, not deleted, in both files. Parity with animals is not literal here — the animals backend's publish.yml and publish-hotfix.yml carry no concurrency block at all — but a publish must never be cancelled or interleaved mid-flight (cdp-build-action bumps the version and pushes a tag, so a lost run can leave the tag ahead of the image), and `cancel-in-progress: false` is the explicit record of that. ins-backend publish.yml:8-11 carries the same block with the same defect

publish.yml's build job keeps its current step order: `Check out code`, then `Set up Java` + `mvn clean verify`, then `DEFRA/cdp-build-action/build@main` (plants publish.yml:27-44). Animals runs verify AFTER the build action and the extra records the difference, but its fix list does not ask for a reorder, the file carries an in-repo comment ruling it deliberate ("Publishing an image whose tests never ran is worse than a slow publish", :31-32), and ins-backend orders it the same way. Do not reorder. Its `if: github.run_number != 1` guard, `name: CDP-build-workflow`, `actions/checkout@v5` pin and the `on:`, `permissions:` and `env:` blocks are all unchanged, as is the `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: "094954420758"` quoting

check-pull-request.yml's pr-validator job is unchanged: its `Run tests with Testcontainers` (`mvn clean verify`) and `Test Docker Image Build` steps, its `actions/checkout@v5` pin and the `java-version-file: '.java-version'` setup all stay as they are (:14-35)

No `.java-version`, `pom.xml`, `README.md`, `Dockerfile` or `src/` change. The README's `### SonarCloud` section (:109-111, "Example SonarCloud configuration are available in the GitHub Action workflows.") is left alone — the animals backend carries that same sentence at README.md:116-118 with SonarCloud live, so it is not drift this increment introduces, and inc-017 is the docs sweep. `.github/dependabot.yml` (inc-013) is not edited: its `github-actions` entry globs `/` and needs no revision when these three files arrive

After the edit, `grep -rn 'queue:' .github/workflows/` and `grep -rn '[$][$][{][{]' .github/workflows/` both return nothing in the plants backend, and `grep -rn '^#' .github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml .github/workflows/publish.yml` returns nothing (no commented-out job or step survives)

All seven files parse as valid YAML with the two-space indentation of their surroundings. No unit or integration test is added: the increment adds no runnable code, and `mvn clean verify` must be green for exactly the reason it is green today. The real proof is the PR's own checks — the loop watches "Publish Branch Image" appear and go green, "SonarCloud Scan" appear as a second check on Check Pull Request, and "E2E Tests" fire on the branch image
openQuestions: Whether the SonarCloud project `DEFRA_trade-imports-plants-backend` exists and `SONAR_TOKEN` is set as a repository or organisation secret on DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-backend. The checkout cannot see either; the pom already carries `<sonar.organization>defra</sonar.organization>` (:30) and the sonar-maven-plugin 5.1.0.4751 (:290-292), and sonarcloud.yml already names the project key, so the config side is ready — but the commented-out block's own preamble said the calls were disabled because the project and token were not set up. If the new SonarCloud Scan check fails at authentication on the first PR, that is a SonarCloud onboarding request, not a defect in this increment.

Whether CDP has provisioned the IAM role `github-trade-imports-plants-backend-build-role` that both reusable workflows assume (workspace publish-multiarch.yml:44-46 and publish-branch.yml log in under `iam-role-name: github-${{ inputs.image-name }}-build-role`). publish.yml already builds this repo through DEFRA/cdp-build-action so the repo is onboarded and defradigital/trade-imports-plants-backend exists, but the branch-image and multi-arch roles are separate grants. A failure at 'Configure AWS credentials' or the Docker Hub login on the first run is an infrastructure request to the CDP platform team.

Whether DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-backend has a `gh-pages` branch and GitHub Pages enabled. The workspace e2e-tests.yml deploys the merged Playwright report to the CALLING repo's Pages (deploy-report job, concurrency group `pages-${{ github.repository }}`, peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4 at :216-217), and the new cleanup-e2e-reports.yml checks out `ref: gh-pages` (workspace cleanup-e2e-reports.yml:23-27) and will fail on a repo that has no such branch. Animals and ins-backend both have one. If the nightly cleanup goes red on a missing ref before the first E2E run has created the branch, that is the ordering, not the YAML.

There is no plants E2E coverage yet — the tests repo's fourth `plants` project arrives later in this backlog — so every plants-backend PR will now run the existing animals suite (three shards, 30-minute timeout) against a stack that includes the plants backend image. That is still real signal (a plants backend that will not boot breaks stack bring-up for the whole suite), and it is what parity asks for, so the plan adds the workflow rather than deferring it. If the team would rather not pay it until the plants specs exist, the change is to delete e2e-tests.yml and cleanup-e2e-reports.yml again — a decision for Sam, not a blocker on this increment.

increments.notes:
Second and last increment in the plants BACKEND for M0. dependsOn inc-013, which creates `.github/dependabot.yml` and deletes `.github/example.dependabot.yml` in this same repo and edits its README — nothing inc-013 touches is edited here, so the dependency is ordering only. The order matters in one direction: inc-013's dependabot entries make the `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'` guards on both new sonarcloud jobs immediately load-bearing rather than theoretical.

Where the increment's own text and the evidence disagree, and how each is resolved:
(1) The detail lists "publish.yml runs mvn clean verify BEFORE the CDP build action" among the differences, but its closing fix list — "Add the three workflows, the arm64 job, restore the sonarcloud calls, read .java-version" — does not ask for a reorder, the skeleton records the difference as "Recorded, not judged", the plants file carries a comment ruling the order deliberate (publish.yml:31-32), and ins-backend publish.yml:36-41 orders it the same way. RULED: keep the plants order. Do not reorder to match animals.
(2) The skeleton also records "Plants pins actions/checkout@v5 where animals pins @v4", again not judged and not in the fix list. RULED: change no action pin, including sonarcloud.yml's lone @v4. Dependabot owns pins from inc-013 onward, and downgrading to match animals would be a regression dressed as parity.
(3) "Parity with the animals backend" is not literal on `concurrency:` — animals has no such block and plants has one in both publish workflows. RULED: keep the blocks, fix them.

One change here goes beyond the extra's detail, deliberately. The plants backend's publish.yml:9 and publish-hotfix.yml:7 carry `$${{ ... }}` concurrency groups and an inert `queue: max`, the identical defect inc-007 fixes in the plants frontend. No backend increment in this backlog covers it, publish.yml is already open in this diff, and publish-hotfix.yml is a three-line edit; the reasoning and the exact target shape are already written out in plans/inc-007.json and are reproduced verbatim in the criteria above. Reviewers checking the diff against filesToTouch will see publish-hotfix.yml listed for exactly this reason. ins-backend carries the same defect and is NOT touched by this increment — raise it separately if it matters.

The three created files are copies, never imports: GitHub requires the caller file to live in the calling repo, so all eleven repos that delegate to the workspace's reusable workflows carry the same 18- and 57-line files and differ only in the image-name line. That duplication is deliberate; the workspace repo holds the one implementation.

What lands where in publish.yml, in order: the concurrency fix at the top of the file, then the build job untouched, then the new `publish-arm64` job, then the new `sonarcloud` job in place of the commented block. Both new jobs take `needs: build`; neither gates the other.

Verification ladder: this is a CI-workflow-only change in a Java repo, so the ladder is `mvn clean verify` and nothing else — `mvn test` alone would skip Failsafe and the integration tests are Testcontainers-backed, so Docker must be running for the rung. There is no maven wrapper at the repo root; `mvn` comes from PATH. No frontend rung applies (no JavaScript is touched), and the fit rung is off the ladder for the same reason it is off inc-002 to inc-013. PROGRAMME-NOTES.md rules the class this increment's open questions fall in: a red check on a CDP role, a SonarCloud token or a missing gh-pages branch is evidence about the platform, not about the change, and a `ci-red` stop on one of them is a question for Sam rather than a code fix.

M0 hygiene: no journey code, no obligation, no page, no copy and no Welsh, and no interaction with the copy-convention or copy-parity tripwires, which live in the frontend and are not armed until the first feature increment. commitPaths is not this plan's concern — PROGRAMME-NOTES.md rules it not applicable under the batch orchestrator, whose land stage stages whatever the increment produced.

increments.notes:
Seven files, all edits, no new file and no behaviour change — M rather than S only because it is more than three files. Two are JSDoc headers, four are markdown docs, one is the repo README. Every one of the five drift sites in the extra's detail was opened at the lines the skeleton finding cites (extract.skeleton.json, readme-and-docs-drift, evidence 'src/server/app/shared/copy.js:6-9; src/server/app/model/obligations/helpers/index.js:1-6; .../add-a-page.md §7; README.md:18-28; .../docs/README.md (The served surface today)') and every one still reads as described.

RULED — the de-duplication owner. The extra says the two 'served surface' passages duplicate each other and both will need updating after the first page; it does not say which survives. The set README wins: it sits beside the code it describes, it already carries the neighbouring 'Adding the first obligation' and 'Gates on the first journey-page increment' sections that the first page increment must read, and the root README is a front door that should link rather than restate. After this increment one passage needs updating when the first page lands, not two.

SCOPE WIDENED, deliberately: src/server/app/docs/README.md carries a third copy of the same emptiness inventory ('The platform below is complete. The high-risk-plants set above it is empty: no obligations, no pages, no flow sections and no task rows'), which the extra does not name. Leaving it would leave the sweep half-done and leave two passages to update after the first page instead of one. Only the duplicated inventory clause goes; the boot-guard warning and the set-guide link stay, because they are that paragraph's actual job. Flagged here so a reviewer comparing the diff against the extra's text sees a ruling rather than a stray file.

SCOPE HELD, deliberately: the copy-convention and copy-parity rules are also restated in add-a-field.md:155-160, add-a-section.md:151-154 and listed in both testing.md files. The extra names add-a-page.md and features.md, and those two are the pair that overlap most (features.md explains the rules; add-a-page.md re-explains them twice, in sections 1 and 4). Sweeping all five would be a docs refactor nobody asked for and would touch two recipes this backlog's first page increment reads verbatim. If a later reader judges add-a-field.md or add-a-section.md misleading, that is a new extra.

SCOPE HELD, deliberately (the hand-off inc-016 left): inc-016's plan notes say 'inc-017 (docs-drift-sweep) owns documentation drift if any of them is later judged misleading', meaning the illustrative JSDoc in model/obligations/helpers/scalar/equals-gate.js:5,35,37, scalar/includes-gate.js:5 and bridge/status/structure/index.js:29 that names purposeInInternalMarket, commercialTransporter, privateTransporter and LAND_TRANSPORT_MODES. Ruled NOT misleading and left alone: they are worked examples of two gate shapes, not claims that any service or obligation exists, and this set owns no obligations yet, so replacing them would mean inventing plants examples the spec has not built. Reconsider once real plants gates land.

DEPENDENCY: runs after inc-016, which edits src/server/app/docs/services.md and the set's docs/services.md and deletes three service folders. No file overlaps with this increment's seven. inc-001 (lighthouse scripts) touches README.md's Lighthouse section, a different section from 'Current state'; if inc-001 has landed by now, expect an edit, not a conflict.

DISCREPANCY (immaterial): the increment's own detail says 'README.md "Current state"' without saying which README, and this repo has three (repo root, src/server/app/docs/, and the set's docs/). The 'Current state' heading exists only in the repo-root README.md (line 18), confirmed by grep, and the skeleton evidence pins it as 'README.md:18-28'. No other disagreement between the increment's text and the spec.

Do not weaken the copy tripwires. copy-parity.test.js's first block asserts that the features directory is still empty and fails deliberately the moment the set owns a feature; copy-convention.test.js is its pair. This increment edits neither, and the docs it edits must keep telling the implementor to fix them rather than skip them.

commitPaths in the target profile is not this increment's concern (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md, 'What the loop commits'): the orchestrator's land stage stages everything the increment produced, so all seven files land in one commit.

npm in this repo is pinned to 11.6.2 (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md); run any install through `npx --yes npm@11.6.2`. This increment needs none. The test:fit:ci rung pins PORT=3053 itself and starts its own webServer, so no rung carries an environment-variable prefix.

Where the increment's own text and the buildable state disagree, the docs settle it. (1) The extra's detail describes the captionSections map as 'Dashboard | About the consignment | Arrival | Destination | Consignment parties'. That is the end state of the map, not what this increment can build: at this point in the chain the only feature folder is journeys/linear/features/dashboard/ (created by inc-018), and captionSections imports page identities, so a section for a page that does not exist would not import. add-a-page.md §6 already assigns the growth to each page increment — 'Once flow/section-captions/ exists, decide the page's caption there: add it to the section it belongs to, or to the bare list in that folder's test. The test should fail until you do one or the other.' Build the dashboard section only, name the other four in the module's doc comment as the target, and let the page increments file themselves. (2) For the same reason the BARE list is empty today; the hub (inc-025) is the first page that must add itself to it. Do not pre-seed either list with page ids that have no page object.

Decided here rather than asked: the test fixture gets its OWN synthetic caption map. The animals repo passes the real set's sectionCaptionOf into the test-side configureJourneyFlow (test/setup-obligation-set.js:16,32), but the plants test/fixtures is explicitly journey-neutral ('Nothing in this directory describes a real journey, and nothing here should be copied into one', test/fixtures/index.js:12-14) and the plants vitest global setup installs that fixture for every test file. Importing the set into the fixture would couple the engine suite to the journey; a fixture-owned map keeps the second call site wired and testable (the kit.test.js criterion) without that coupling.

Chain: inc-018 creates the dashboard feature and, per add-a-page.md §6, places dashboardPage in flow.js sections — this increment's coverage test and the captionSections entry both depend on that. inc-020 and inc-021 have already re-armed copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js against the landed dashboard feature, so copy-parity.test.js here is an edit to a restored file (an async modulePairs() builder returning the per-feature pairs followed by the shared pairs), not to the armed tripwire. If inc-018's dashboard template already imports the macro, this increment only corrects the class and placement rather than adding the call.

The fit spec is the only rung that proves the routes.js call site, and the last rung (test:fit:ci) needs the stack up; it pins PORT=3053 itself, so no rung carries an environment-variable prefix (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md, 'Verification ladder').

CHAIN POSITION. By the time this builds: the dashboard page serves '/' with the create POST, the per-status actions and the ?deleted=1 banner; section captions are wired; the Overview hub serves '/notifications/{journeyId}' with GROUPS and taskRows []; the delete-notification confirmation page serves '/notifications/{journeyId}/delete'; and the e2e-plants-project-scaffold increment has added the plants Playwright project, the plants base URLs, navigateToPlantsFrontend on BasePage, PlantsDashboardPage, the AUTH_TARGETS plants entry and tests/e2e/features/plants/dashboard-smoke.spec.ts. Nothing in the plants frontend or backend is touched here.

DISCREPANCY, resolved in the spec's favour. journey-spec.json pages[dashboard].startAction says the create POST 'begins the opening run and redirects to commodity-type'. The commodity-type page lands in the increment AFTER this one, and the spec's own pages[hub].notes says the hub is 'placed in start so the create POST has somewhere to land' — with RUN_STEPS still empty, nextRunTarget falls through to hubPath(journeyId). The dashboard increment's ruled criterion pins the redirect at hubPath for now. So this spec asserts the create lands on the Overview. When the commodity-type increment appends the first RUN_STEPS entry and repoints the redirect, the e2e-commodity-section spec must update this spec's create assertion to 'lands on commodity-type, then reaches the Overview' — that is a named follow-up for that increment, not a defect here.

DISCREPANCY, resolved. The extra asks the start spec to 'sign in via the Defra ID stub ... with page objects'. No plants sign-in page object is created: page-objects/auth/sign-in-page.ts drives the stub for every service, the scaffold increment already ruled a plants copy would drift, and the stub is configured for the plants origin.

DECISION, recorded headless. tests/e2e/features/plants/dashboard-smoke.spec.ts is deleted and its assertions become this spec's '@smoke'-tagged first test. That file was the project canary written before the start section existed and it asserts exactly what the extra asks this spec's dashboard test to assert — heading, start button, no error summary. Keeping both would leave two specs over one render for no added coverage. The plants project keeps a @smoke-tagged test either way.

REFERENCE FORMAT. Under the workspace stack the plants frontend runs the real records adapter, so journeyId and referenceNumber are the same value and the reference has NO type-code prefix: {YY}-{XXXXXX}. Assert the pattern, never a literal and never 'GBN-AG-'. The prefix extra sits at the end of the chain with gate 'sam' and will change this pattern when the type code is agreed; the spec's regex is the one place to update.

SESSION SCOPING IS WHAT MAKES THE DELETE TESTS DETERMINISTIC. Known journey ids live in yar, and the reused worker storage state carries only the 'sid' auth cookie, so every Playwright context starts with an empty dashboard. Assert on the card for this test's own reference rather than on notificationCards counts, so a change to session reuse cannot silently turn a real failure green.

THE STACK MUST BE UP IN DEV MODE. `tim docker dev`, so :3003 serves this branch's build of the high-risk-plants set. A plain stack run pulls defradigital/trade-imports-plants-frontend:latest, which has no set built, no dashboard and no hub, and every test in this spec reds for that reason alone. Cross-repo branch parity (CLAUDE.md rule 2): the tests-repo branch carries the SAME name as the plants frontend branch, because the stack probes each repo for a branch-tagged image and falls back to :latest on a mismatch.

LOCATOR RULES THAT BITE HERE. (1) The card's reference heading level is govuk-frontend's summary-card default and is not spec'd, so locate the card by its reference text inside .govuk-summary-card, never by heading level. (2) 'Return to dashboard', 'Back' and the delete page's 'No, return to dashboard' are all links styled as buttons or plain links whose accessible names are substrings of longer names elsewhere on the page — use exact: true, as BasePage.linkBack's comment already explains for the phase-banner 'give your feedback' collision. (3) Dashboard action names carry the visually-hidden suffix `notification {reference}`, so the accessible name is 'Resume notification {reference}', not 'Resume'.

AXE IS NOT THIS INCREMENT'S JOB. The plants frontend's in-repo fit specs own the accessibility checks for the dashboard, hub and delete pages (each of those increments lands an AxeBuilder check). The plants Playwright project's testMatch covers only tests/e2e/features/plants/, so no a11y spec is added here and no '@a11y' tag is used.

WHAT THE CHAIN HAS LANDED BY THE TIME THIS BUILDS. The dashboard increment created the first feature folder (journeys/linear/features/dashboard/), put dashboardPage in flow.js sections as { id: 'start', pages: [dashboardPage] }, registered the create POST at /notifications, and — under d-084, which withdrew the two copy-tripwire restore extras — rewrote copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js in the same commit so both walk the features folder. There is therefore NO tripwire to trip here and no armed emptiness assertion: this feature's copy/ folder and en/cy pair are picked up automatically and neither file is edited. The unauthorised-view-copy-and-stack-check chore moved the unauthorised view into sharedCopy; wire-section-captions created flow/section-captions/ with the dashboard section only and passed sectionCaption in both configureJourneyFlow call sites, and its plan explicitly leaves 'About the consignment' for this increment ('name the other four in the module's doc comment as the target, and let the page increments file themselves'). The e2e-plants-project-scaffold extra scaffolded the plants Playwright project in the tests repo and touches nothing here. The hub increment created features/hub/ with GROUPS carrying four captions, taskRows [], the five-status map, all four row-building rules written in full, copy.rows as an empty object, and flow/task-rows.test.js. The exemplar-hub chore closed the hub placeholder in add-a-page.md; the delete-notification-page chore copied that confirmation page from animals; the e2e-start-section spec covers the dashboard and overview in the tests repo.

THE THREE-PART CHANGE IS THE SHAPE OF THIS INCREMENT. docs/README.md:84-102 is load-bearing: three boot guards enforce one joint invariant, so the obligation (obligations/sections/commodity.js plus the manifest), the page that names it in meta.collects (dispatchPages), and the feature binding that owns it (evaluation.js plus the features/evaluation.js barrel) must land in the same commit. Two of them alone do not boot: assertFullCoverage throws 'Obligations collected by no page', assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage throws 'obligations owned by no feature', and a structurally identical copy of the obligation object fails with 'must import its obligation object from the manifest'. add-a-field.md's step ordering describes the intermediate red states as expected while you work; the commit is atomic.

WHAT THIS INCREMENT IS THE FIRST OF, and therefore what it creates rather than edits: the first obligation, so obligations/sections/ is a new folder; the first feature binding, so featureEvaluationBindings stops being a frozen empty array; the first dispatchPages entry; the first flow section after the dashboard's; the first task row; the first RUN_STEPS entry; the first caption section after the dashboard's; the first set-owned service; and the first collecting controller. Every one of those registration modules already exists and is empty — features/index.js, features/evaluation.js, flow/flow.js, flow/task-rows.js, flow/run.js, obligations/index.js — so each is an edit, not a create. flow/task-rows.test.js and flow/section-captions/ exist too (the hub and wire-section-captions increments created them) and are edits.

WHAT THIS INCREMENT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. (1) The entry guard stays inert. flow/entry-guard.js gains only the exported pure helper hasCommittedNotificationAnswers, which this page's back link needs and which the animals set also keeps in that module; entryGuardTarget is still async () => null, and guardedJourneyPath, the action-slug set and the redirect are the restore-entry-guard extra's, which follows this increment and is keyed to this page's identity. Do not restore the guard early and do not add an interim one. (2) contract.test.js and obligations/coverage.test.js are NOT recreated here even though add-a-page.md §9 and add-a-field.md §3 say the first collecting controller recreates contract.test.js — the restore-contract-and-coverage-tests extra owns both and is anchored after restore-entry-guard. Where the recipe and the extras decomposition disagree, the decomposition wins, exactly as it did for the tripwires on the dashboard. (3) No EXEMPLAR PLACEHOLDER is closed: add-a-page.md's and features.md's are the exemplar-single-field-page extra's, which names this page as the exemplar; add-a-field.md's several-field exemplar waits for a richer feature; add-a-section.md's waits for the commodities group; the README table waits for exemplar-readme-table. Do not edit a recipe here. (4) FLOW_ONLY_KEYS stays empty until the declaration page. (5) configureAnswersForRead stays identity until the restore-answers-read-sanitiser extra. (6) The check-answers card and the notification mapper are untouched: no check-answers feature exists yet, and the plants NotificationDto has no home for commodityType (notification-mapper projects the reference and nothing else), so leave the mapper unchanged — an explicit omission assertion belongs with the mapper's own test, which the first mapped field creates.

SPEC vs SPEC, and the reconciliations this plan makes (the later ruling wins in each). (1) journey-spec.json pages[commodity-type].notes, as ruled at d-023/c-013, describes a govukWarningText above the radios and a reconcileEntriesAt branch in POST that redirects to commodities?removed=<n>. commodityLines, the commodities list page and category.input.valuesByCommodityType do not exist until the commodities collection increment, so none of that is buildable here, and the same note supplies the fallback for exactly this state: 'When the value is unchanged or no lines exist the POST behaves as any single-question page.' The warning, the reconcile branch, the redirect through kit.withChangeContext and the four controller tests d-029 names (the drop, the keep, the unchanged no-op and the redirect) are the commodities collection increment's to add to THIS controller — it must edit this file, not build a second one. Say so in that increment's plan. (2) behaviour set-owned-commodities-service says the service is 'Created by the commodities increment', while d-073 (later, D6) forbids the commodityType list from living in a copy or obligation literal. d-073 wins: the service is created here with commodityTypes() only. (3) d-073 places the timing-window constants 'beside the arrival-details feature', which does not exist; they land as a sibling module under features/ so the copy can read them without a half-empty feature folder. (4) add-a-page.md §4 still says section captions are not wired — wire-section-captions made that false and corrected the doc; follow the corrected text.

THE ANIMALS SHAPE TO COPY, NEVER IMPORT. This page is plants-only (journey-spec.json pages[commodity-type].animals.relation and obligations[commodityType].animals.relation), so no copy is inherited and nothing corresponds one-for-one — animals branches on reasonForImport, not on a commodity type. What is copied is the SHAPE of a single-question radios page: repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend/src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-reason/ (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, evaluation.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.test.js, import-reason.fit.spec.js) — its legend-as-heading template with the caption above, its options-from-a-service render helper, its per-option hints from copy keyed by value, and its GET/POST ordering. Two differences the spec requires: validation is requiredOneOf, not oneOf (lenient-page-validation names commodityType as one of the three plants pages that require at page level, where animals import-reason does not); and the option labels come from copy rather than from the service, because the plants service holds values only. The state-dependent back link copies the animals origin controller's backLinkFor (live-animals features/origin/controller.js:160-167) with hubPath/dashboardPath, not the animals page's own copy.

LIGHTHOUSE. Nothing under scripts/lighthouse/ is edited. The lighthouse-scripts fix derives the URL list from allRoutes and the report name from the route path, so this page joins the audit by being registered; its prerequisites are met by the existing draft seed shape and it needs no SKIPPED / FILLED_BY / QUERY entry, because its route carries no path parameter beyond the journey id.

NPM AND THE LADDER. The repo pins npm 11.6.2 via packageManager; run any install through `npx --yes npm@11.6.2`. test:high-risk-plants covers only vitest under the set, so the bridge/obligation-source.js edit and any L1 test are proved by the `test` rung. test:fit:ci pins PORT=3053 itself and needs the workspace stack up — no rung carries an environment-variable prefix. commitPaths is not this increment's concern: under the batch orchestrator the land stage stages whatever the increment produced.

increments.title: Restore the entry guard with commodity-type as the entry page
increments.detail: flow/entry-guard.js exports entryGuardTarget = async () => null, so routes.js's onPreHandler never redirects and any deep link reaches a mid-journey page. Restore the documented shape: a guardedJourneyPath filter that ignores anything outside /notifications/<id>/, the create path, the amend/cancel-amend/copy/delete action slugs and the commodity-type page and its sub-paths; admit when openingRunStarted for that journey in this session OR hasCommittedNotificationAnswers; otherwise redirect to commodity-type. A bounced user saving commodity-type continues to the hub, not into the run. Tests in flow/entry-guard.test.js plus a fit case. Evidence: skeleton entry-guard-inert (entry-guard.js:1-5; routes.js:62-65; set README 'Gates on the first journey-page increment'); behaviour entry-guard.

A journey whose only stored answer is a flow-only key such as declaration therefore reads as fresh — flow-only keys are session state, never manifest obligations (journey-flow-and-gates.md 'Flow-only values use the session's flow-only store, not canonical obligation fulfilment')

The controller and flow import the same object'). journey-spec.json page commodity-type: slug 'commodity-type', notes 'The journey entry page: the entry guard redirects here, the opening run starts here, and its identity is what the restored entry guard needs'

A journey the guard bounced does not resume the opening run when it saves commodity-type: kit.nextTarget finds inOpeningRun false, so runTarget is null and nextInSection falls through to hubPath (shared/kit.js:109-120; flow/navigation.js:27-36; journey-flow-and-gates.md 'That is the accepted rule for a returning user without run state. Only a notification created in this session sequences through RUN_STEPS'). Prove it, do not assume it

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE. The commodity-type page increment lands immediately before this one and creates features/commodity-type/ (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, evaluation.js, the copy pair, controller.test.js, commodity-type.fit.spec.js) and registers it in features/index.js, features/evaluation.js, flow/flow.js, flow/task-rows.js and flow/run.js RUN_STEPS. This increment creates no feature and registers nothing: routes.js already wires entryGuardTarget through configureJourneyFlow and calls it from onPreHandler. The dashboard increment made the create POST the single caller of beginOpeningRun and redirects to the hub; the hub increment completes the run. So every notification started in-session already carries the openingRun cookie and sails through the restored guard — the dashboard, hub and delete-notification fit specs must stay green untouched. If any of them goes red, the guard is over-reaching; fix the guard, not the spec.

THE SHAPE TO COPY (never import from animals, never centralise). repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend/src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js is the mirror, line for line: JOURNEY_PREFIX from BASE, an ACTION_SLUGS Set, guardedJourneyPath splitting journeyId from the rest of the path and rejoining the slug with '/', the userEntered helper over obligationByName + SYSTEM_POPULATED, hasCommittedNotificationAnswers over isAnswered, and entryGuardTarget checking openingRunStarted then answers. Swap animals' originPage for the plants commodityTypePage; nothing else differs. Both docblocks in the animals file are load-bearing prose — write the plants equivalents, pointing at ../../../docs/journey-flow-and-gates.md, and add no other commentary.

THE BACK-LINK OVERLAP — read this before editing. The commodity-type page's spec backLink is 'hub when the notification has any committed user answer, else dashboard (animals origin-back-link rule — this is the plants entry page)', and animals implements exactly that by importing hasCommittedNotificationAnswers from flow/entry-guard.js (animals features/origin/controller.js:20, 158-161). The commodity-type increment lands first, so one of two states greets you. (a) It already added hasCommittedNotificationAnswers (and its userEntered helper) to entry-guard.js and imports it — then this increment adds only guardedJourneyPath and the real entryGuardTarget, and features/commodity-type/controller.js is not in the diff. (b) It implemented the back-link rule locally in the controller — then fold that local predicate into entry-guard.js, repoint the controller's import at it, add features/commodity-type/controller.js to the diff as an edit, and say in the PR that the plan under-listed by one file. Either way the increment ends with exactly ONE definition of hasCommittedNotificationAnswers, exported from flow/entry-guard.js. Check first; do not assume (a).

THE `copy` ACTION SLUG IS BUILT EVEN THOUGH NOTHING SERVES IT. Copy as new and its banner are parked (d-062 / behaviour notification-actions-after-submission), so /notifications/<id>/copy has no route in plants today. Keep 'copy' in ACTION_SLUGS anyway: the extra's detail, the set README gate and the adopted entry-guard behaviour all name the same four slugs, and the exemption is forward-looking, not dead policy. Do not drop it to satisfy a coverage or dead-code observation, and do not add a route for it.

SPEC vs DOCS, where they disagree (the spec wins, per PROGRAMME-NOTES 'Where the spec and an increment's own text disagree, the spec wins'):
1. add-a-page.md:39-42 and docs/README.md:105-109 both say the first journey page increment restores the guard 'in the same increment'. The adopted behaviour entry-guard says the opposite — 'restoring it is a declared backlog extra anchored after the commodity-type page because it needs that page's identity' — and backlog-extras.json anchors this extra 'after page:commodity-type'. The backlog shape wins; correcting that add-a-page.md sentence is part of this increment, which is why the doc is in filesToTouch.
2. The extra's detail says 'Tests in flow/entry-guard.test.js plus a fit case'. Animals keeps its guard tests inside flow/opening-run.test.js. Follow the extra: a dedicated flow/entry-guard.test.js. The plants set has no opening-run.test.js to join.
3. The extra's detail and the README describe the same guard in different words; where the wording differs, docs/journey-flow-and-gates.md 'Opening run and entry guard' is the fuller statement and the six bullets there are the requirement.

ENGINE FACTS VERIFIED IN THE PLANTS REPO, so nothing here needs inventing: shared/paths.js exports BASE (the empty string), pagePath, hubPath, createPath and dashboardPath; flow/run-state.js exports openingRunStarted, inOpeningRun, RUN_ACTIVE and RUN_COMPLETE; engine/read.js:69 exports get(request, h) returning { journey, answers, ... }; engine/journey.js:54-72 currentJourney throws Boom.notFound() when there is no journeyId or no record and adds an unknown-but-real journey to knownJourneys — which is why the exempt-path test must pass a request with no journeyId and expect no throw, and why the fit deep link from a second session resolves rather than 404s; bridge/obligation-source.js exports obligationByName and SYSTEM_POPULATED (an empty Set in this repo, plus 'systemPopulatedField' merged in by the test fixture — harmless, commodityType is not in it); lib/answered.js exports isAnswered; engine/test-support.js exports journeyRequest and stubH (journeyRequest sets no `path`, so pass one through overrides); engine/store.js exports store.create, store.seedAnswers and store.clear; the set's SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES (config.js) renames all three cookies, so configureSession must run before any request state literal is built.

DEPCRUISE. flow/entry-guard.js importing ../features/commodity-type/page.js stays inside sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/, so journey-isolation and set-isolation are untouched; engine/, bridge/, lib/, shared/ and flow/ are all L2 APIs a set may consume (sets-not-l1 forbids only routes.js, obligation-purity.js and the two root convention tests). page.js imports nothing, so no cycle forms with the controller. Run lint (it chains lint:arch) rather than reasoning about it.

NOT THIS INCREMENT: FLOW_ONLY_KEYS stays empty until the declaration page; configureAnswersForRead stays identity (the restore-answers-read-sanitiser extra); sectionCaption is the wire-section-captions extra's; the repo-root README 'Current state' and the set README 'The served surface today' belong to exemplar-readme-table; the add-a-page.md EXEMPLAR PLACEHOLDER blocks belong to exemplar-single-field-page.

THE ONE REAL TRAP, AND WHERE IT DIVERGES FROM ANIMALS. The animals repo's test/setup-obligation-set.js wires the REAL live-animals set globally, so its contract.test.js gets the real manifest for free. The plants repo's setup does the opposite: test/setup-obligation-set.js calls installFixture(), which configures a synthetic journey-neutral set (the engine is journey-agnostic and its tests must not depend on the installed set — sets/high-risk-plants/docs/obligation-model.md, 'The Vitest suite does NOT wire this set'). bridge/obligation-source.js reads the CONFIGURED set, so a contract.test.js copied verbatim from animals would resolve commodityType against the fixture, find nothing, compare an empty set with an empty set and pass while proving nothing. Configure the plants set in beforeAll and put the fixture back with installFixture() in afterAll. The two non-vacuity criteria exist for the same reason — this file is the one place in the suite where a green run can be a lie.

THE TABLE STAYS MANUAL — A DELIBERATE NON-CHANGE. behaviour contract-test-table says the first collecting controller recreates the file 'and every later collecting page adds a case', and add-a-page.md, add-a-section.md and add-a-collection.md all say the same in the same words: 'A new controller that is absent from the table does not make the test fail, so add the case even when the suite is green.' openQuestions: Where the multi-page group's shared Playwright helper lives. `journeys/linear/features/commodities/fit/axe.js` is a Playwright-only helper sitting under `src/`, where every scope config classifies it as production source: `sonar-project.properties:18-21` and `.sonarcloud.properties:6-9` both set `sonar.sources=src/` with `sonar.test.inclusions` limited to `src/**/*.test.js,src/**/*.fit.spec.js` (which `fit/axe.js` does not match), and `vitest.config.js:25` sets `coverage.include: ['src/**/*.js']` while the suite exclude drops `.fit.spec.js` — so the helper is the only Playwright module measured for coverage, landing in lcov as 0/8 lines of 'main' code. It is also why `JSON_INDENT` exists at `axe.js:11` (eslint.config.js:45-47 applies no-magic-numbers to `src/server/**/*.js` while exempting `*.test.js`/`*.spec.js`). Both candidate fixes fall outside this target's commitPaths (`src/server/app`, `package.json`, `.github`, `scripts`, `docs`, `README.md`, `.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json`): moving it to the repo-root `fit/` directory beside `fit/sign-in.js` writes a file the loop cannot stage, and excluding `src/**/fit/**` means editing `sonar-project.properties`, `.sonarcloud.properties` and `vitest.config.js`, none of which are commitable here either. Needs a repo-config decision plus a commitPaths widening before it can be actioned.

Whether the duplicated preamble between `commodities/fit/details.fit.spec.js` and `commodities/fit/list.fit.spec.js` should be extracted. The two files share the same eight imports, the COMMODITY_TYPE_URL / DETAILS_URL / DETAILS_EDIT_URL / LIST_URL regexes, SEED_POTATOES, MARIS_PIPER, `saveAndContinue`, `fieldNamed` and two already-diverged copies of `startAtDetails`. Extracting a `fit/journey.js` beside `axe.js` would add a second shared helper in exactly the location the axe.js question above says is misclassified as production source, so the two must be settled together; and the workspace rule 'feature folders are independent by design — declare duplication, don't extract' argues for leaving spec-local duplication alone. Settle the axe.js placement first, then decide whether a shared journey helper joins it.
