openQuestions: The increment detail asks for "Tests in the set plus a fit case", and no fit spec was added. The fit suite runs with STUB_MODE=true (playwright.config.js:65) against the static STUB_BOOK (services/address-book/stub/index.js:14-28), whose every record is minted with deleted:false (stub/from-row.js:14) and which has no write path; the picker only commits an id that already resolves (features/place-of-destination/controller.js:148-158). A dangling or soft-deleted reference is therefore unproducible through the browser today, so the fit case is dropped as unreachable rather than silently unmet. The rendered-page proof ("a deleted record renders Not provided on CYA") is already scheduled downstream in the e2e-destination-section extra (sets/high-risk-plants/spec/backlog-extras.json, anchored after key:restore-answers-read-sanitiser), which runs against the real address book where deletion is producible. Confirm that is where it lands, or raise a separate increment to give stub mode a deletion affordance (a deleted:true STUB_BOOK record plus searchStub filtering it out, and a way to reach it from an already-committed answer) if a frontend-local fit case is wanted.

Placement constraint for any future fit case here: playwright.config.js:47-49 scopes the features project testDir to journeys/linear/features, and vitest.config.js:17 excludes *.fit.spec.js only under features/**. A fit spec placed under journeys/linear/parties/ would be skipped by Playwright and collected — and fail — by vitest. It must go under features/place-of-destination/.

increments.title: Sync the ported engine and platform with the animals frontend's refactoring since the port base
increments.detail: The plants frontend ported its journey-agnostic engine and platform from the animals frontend at origin/main @2ed89aef (plants commit dba9c35, 2026-09-05, 'bring the plants frontend up to the trade-imports shape'). Animals has kept refactoring those layers since. Diff the common areas between animals main as it stands when this increment runs and 2ed89aef, and port every engine-level change forward into plants so the two engines match again. The common areas are src/server/app minus sets/ (analysis, auth, bridge, docs, engine, flow, lib, model, services, shared, routes.js and the app-level test files), the auth, signout, common, config, client and plugins layers, test/ and test-helpers/, scripts/, the platform docs, and the build and lint configuration (package.json and its overrides block, webpack, vitest, playwright, dependency-cruiser, sonar-project.properties). Evidence: `git -C repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend log 2ed89aef..origin/main -- . ':!src/server/app/sets'` lists the commits; `diff -rq --exclude=sets --exclude=node_modules` across the two src/server/app trees shows the drift. Raised by Sam on 2026-09-07 because animals refactoring will otherwise leave plants on a fork of the engine.

acceptanceCriteria: The increment starts by recording the sync window: the animals commit range 2ed89aef..<animals main SHA at build time>, restricted to paths outside src/server/app/sets/. That range and the SHA it ends at are written into the set README under a 'Engine sync' heading, so the next sync knows its base. If the range is empty the increment lands that note alone and stops.

Every commit in the range is classified as engine (journey-agnostic: engine/, model/, bridge/, lib/, shared/, flow/, services/ ports and codecs, auth, config, plugins, test harness, build and lint config, platform docs) or journey (anything whose behaviour is only meaningful for live animals: parity-dr1 copy and page changes, set-specific fulfilments, mapper-a field mappings, live-animals fixtures). Engine commits are ported; journey commits are not. The classification is listed in the PR description, one line per commit, so a reviewer can disagree with a line rather than re-derive the split.

After the port, `diff -rq --exclude=sets --exclude=node_modules` between the two src/server/app trees shows only the deliberate plants divergences: the synthetic fixture manifest wiring under test/fixtures/ and test/setup-obligation-set.js, the removed commodity-reference seam and the removed document-uploads, document-types and certification-purposes services, journey-neutral naming in docs and JSDoc, and routes.js pointing at the high-risk-plants set. Each remaining difference is named in the PR description with the reason it stays.

No file under src/server/app/sets/ is touched except the set README's 'Engine sync' note and any recipe doc that a ported engine change made wrong. No journey copy, obligation, page or fulfilment is added, and nothing is imported from the animals repo — the port is a copy, declared, never a dependency (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md 'Consistency with animals, without sharing').

Tests animals added to the engine since the base (for example a characterisation, golden or contract test) come across pointed at the plants fixture manifest, not at live-animals data, and pass. A test that cannot be made journey-neutral is left out and named in the PR description with the reason.

The obligation-purity guard, copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js are not weakened. If animals changed those tripwires, the plants versions take the same change while keeping their per-feature checks for the high-risk-plants set.

No behaviour change in the plants journey: every plants feature's own unit tests and *.fit.spec.js pass unchanged, and the plants E2E project in the tests repo (`npm --prefix ~/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace/repos/trade-imports-animals-tests run test:docker-compose -- --project=plants`) passes against the synced frontend with the stack up.
Every rung of the ladder is green, including lint:arch (dependency-cruiser) with no new violations and format:check.
openQuestions: Whether this sync should recur — one increment at the end of the build catches the drift up to that day, but animals will keep moving. If Sam wants it repeatable, the 'Engine sync' README note is the base for a follow-on chore extra; a shared package is ruled out by the no-sharing rule.

increments.notes:
Added by the orchestrator on 2026-09-07 at Sam's request ('add something to the end of the increment backlog which will be to diff against animals repo for the common areas — there's been refactoring in animals this will need to sync up with'). Not in the spec's backlog-extras.json; if the backlog is ever regenerated from the spec this increment must be re-added or the extra written into backlog-extras.json first.

PORT BASE: plants commit dba9c35 says it ported animals origin/main @2ed89aef. On 2026-09-07 the animals checkout's main is still at 2ed89aef, so the drift is on animals origin or on branches not yet merged; the increment measures the range when it runs, not now. Engine files already differ in 80 places between the two checkouts (5,862 differing lines outside sets/), but most of that is the shape commit's deliberate journey-neutral rewrite of the engine tests, not animals refactoring — the classification step exists to keep those apart.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES the sync must not undo (from dba9c35's own message): the engine tests run against a synthetic fixture manifest under test/fixtures/ with structural names (scalarField, statusToggle, branchSelector, compositeBlockOne, itemCollection, nestedCollection); the commodity-reference seam (commodityCodeFor, speciesLabel, typeTextForId) was removed; the repo names no journey domain outside the tests-repo reference and the recipes' guard rails. Animals-only folders today that stay out: services/certification-purposes, services/document-types, services/document-uploads, notification-mapper/mapper-a, notification-mapper/shared, notification-mapper/commodity-reference.js, and the mapper-a contract tests. Document uploads are also parked per the epic (PROGRAMME-NOTES.md standing rulings).

ORDER: dependsOn inc-058, the last unblocked increment, so it runs once every plants feature has landed and the engine is synced exactly once against a finished set. It deliberately does not depend on the three gated extras (inc-059 to inc-061): they are born blocked awaiting Sam's rulings, and a sync that waited on a ruling would never run. If one of them lands first and touches engine files, this increment absorbs the diff.

SIZE: L is a guess. The range is unmeasured; a handful of engine commits is an M, a rewrite of the obligation helpers (EUDPA-360 shape) is an L, and if animals has moved the persistence contract it may need to be split by layer. The implementor should say which in the PR description rather than force one PR.
